observe: Waveform: on a cycle with io.update.valid = 1 and io.update.usefulCntValid = 0, writeBuffers(b).io.write.head.bits.bitmask at IttageTable.scala:215 has bit 1 set (value = all-ones minus bit 0, e.g. 0x...FFFE for the 29+tagLen-bit entry) and bit 1 of writePort.bits.entry (line 213) is the DontCare-derived io.update.usefulCnt. Follow-up: during a sweep (usefulCanReset = 1, line 182) the same bitmask is 0x1 and the SRAM's usefulCnt column never changes, so ittage_us_tick_reset (line 264) keeps firing while providerUsefulCnt in IttageMeta never returns to 0 for entries that were set useful; allocation candidates (Ittage.scala:296-301, usefulCnt saturate-negative) dry up. Corroboration: upstream commit b657b5fe8 'fix(ittage): derive useful counter masks from entry fields (#6569)' rebuilds the mask from the Bundle field itself and states 'Previous implementation does not reset useful counter due to deriving bitmask through fixed location'; ff68f3c5a does not contain it.
trace_notes: Guards checked: (1) update.valid and usefulCanReset are mutually exclusive by construction (line 182: usefulCanReset = !(req.fire || update.valid) && needReset), so the Mux at 190-194 never sees both; priority all > noUs > us > none is therefore total and unambiguous. (2) writePort.valid (line 212) = (update.valid && bankMask) || usefulCanReset and setIdx (line 214) = Mux(usefulCanReset, resetSet, updateIdx) are consistent with the mask selection in every combination. (3) Data word during a sweep: usefulCnt = SaturateNegative (line 250-251), other fields are stale update values but masked out; during an update: all fields from io.update, usefulCnt = io.update.usefulCnt. The failure is not in the Mux or the data word but in the encoding of the two partial masks: they are built from fixed bit indices [0, UsefulCntWidth) while the Bundle places paddingBit, not usefulCnt, at bit 0. The comment at Bundles.scala:47 ('useful bit needs to be at the lowest bit') documents the intended convention, and the field declared after it breaks it. With UsefulCntWidth = 1 the off-by-one is exact: usBitmask = {paddingBit}, noUsBitmask = {everything incl. usefulCnt}.
